title: A bill to amend the Bill Emerson Good Samaritan Food Donation Act to improve the program, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
This act expands liability protections for the donation of food and grocery products.

Specifically, the act expands the liability protections to include donations of an apparently fit grocery product or apparently wholesome food

  • for which the recipient is charged a good Samaritan reduced price that is no greater than the cost of handling, administering, harvesting, processing, packaging, transporting, and distributing the food or product; or
  • that is donated directly to a needy individual at zero cost by a retail grocer, wholesaler, agricultural producer, agricultural processor, agricultural distributor, restaurant, caterer, school food authority, or institution of higher education.

summary.headline: A law that widens legal protection for people and businesses that donate food and groceries to those in need.
summary.what_it_does: The act expands liability protections for food and grocery donations. Protection now covers food sold at a reduced "good Samaritan" price that does not exceed the cost of handling, processing, packaging, transporting, and distributing it. It also covers food given directly to needy individuals at no cost by certain food businesses and institutions.

who_it_affects.how: They gain liability protection when they donate food or groceries, including at a reduced price that covers handling and distribution costs.
Farms, food processors, and agricultural distributors gain liability protection when they donate food directly to needy individuals at no cost.
They gain liability protection when they donate food directly to needy individuals at no cost.

who_it_affects.group: Schools and colleges with food service
who_it_affects.how: School food authorities and institutions of higher education gain liability protection when they donate food directly to needy individuals at no cost.

who_it_affects.group: Needy individuals who receive donated food
who_it_affects.how: More food and grocery donations may be covered under the expanded protections, which may make donors more willing to give food at no cost or at a reduced price.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The act became law on January 5, 2023. The official summary does not list a separate effective date for its provisions.
